subject: Retention provenance & sample artifacts for SOC 2/ISO evidence
messages:
From: Lauren Finch <redbank-auditor@assurify.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-05-03T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Evidence request: retention provenance & deletion samples (SOC 2 / ISO)

Hi Jonas,

Assurify is running the RedBank SOC 2 readiness check and we need artifacts that demonstrate retention/residency provenance and deletion proof for a sample tenant. Specifically we are asking for: 

- A mapping of data categories to retention TTLs and physical/geographic residency (where data is stored and for how long).
- A small sample export showing a tenant lifecycle: creation, updates, and the delete/erasure action (with timestamps and traceability to the delete job).
- Any cross-region replication notes or exceptions (if data moved between geozones).
- A short description of the process used to verify a deletion (how you prove bits are erased and what logs are produced).

Please attach example artifacts (PDFs/CSV/log snippets) for one production tenant (we'll use tenant-8472 as the sample) and include expected TTL values for tokens, caches, and persisted objects. We prefer not to receive a full data export — just the minimal artifacts to validate controls.

Can you confirm by EOD 5/7 whether you can provide these artifacts and a 30-min call next week to walk through them?

Thanks,
Lauren Finch
Senior Auditor, Assurify
lauren.finch@assurify.com

---
Note: this is a formal evidence request for SOC 2 / ISO readiness.
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-05-03T09:45:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Evidence request: retention provenance & deletion samples (SOC 2 / ISO)

Team — forwarding an external auditor request (RedBank via Assurify). They want mapping + a small sample proving deletion for tenant-8472. Auditor asked for confirmation by EOD 5/7 and a 30-min walkthrough next week.

Key asks: TTLs for different data categories (KV cache vs persisted store), residency mapping, sample delete log snippet, and the verification approach. Keep attachments minimal.

Can Soojin and Vivek assemble the artifacts and a short narrative? Marissa: if there are contractual/regulatory nuances for RedBank (financial), please flag anything we need to escalate.

I'll own the call scheduling once we have materials to share.

Thanks,
Jonas
Director, Compliance Engineering
Redwood Inference
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-05-04T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Evidence request: retention provenance & deletion samples (SOC 2 / ISO)

Jonas —

Attached are the artifacts we can produce quickly for tenant-8472: redwood-retention-mapping-2025-05-07.pdf (compact mapping of object classes -> TTLs -> physical region), and sample-delete-log-tenant-8472.csv (sanitized rows showing creation_time, last_update, delete_request_time, delete_job_id, deletion_complete_time).

Notes (summary):
- TTL mapping: short-lived caches (KV cache) are TTLed at 24 hours by default but may be configured per-tenant; long-term persisted objects (user prompts, embeddings) have configured retention at 365 days by default for hosted customers, with a tenant override for enterprise tenants. See attached PDF for exact object-level mapping used in our serving runtime.
- Residency: primary storage is in us-west1 for this tenant; cross-region replication to us-east1 only occurs for Dedicated customers with explicit config (not the case for tenant-8472). The mapping PDF has a per-bucket residency column.
- Sample delete: our delete flow issues a delete_request (API, with requestor id), enqueues a delete job that boundaries across services (user metadata, object storage, KV caches). The CSV includes delete_job_id and a gzipped-storage-object-ref column (we redact full object names for confidentiality).

We purposely include the delete_job_id and timestamp chain so an auditor can trace the lifecycle. The actual data object blobs are not included. For verification we provide the job trace and S3/ObjectStore lifecycle events.

I also included a small TTL diagram (kv-cache-ttl-diagram.png) showing where cached items are kept and the eviction/TTL enforcement point.

If they want cryptographic proof-of-erasure (e.g., hash comparisons pre/post), that's a heavier lift — we can produce hash manifests for a narrow subset but we'll need approval from product & privacy.

--
Soojin Lee
Senior Product Engineer, Platform
Redwood Inference
(Attachment stubs: redwood-retention-mapping-2025-05-07.pdf, sample-delete-log-tenant-8472.csv, kv-cache-ttl-diagram.png)
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-05-05T14:52:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Evidence request: retention provenance & deletion samples (SOC 2 / ISO)

Adding a few control/verification notes for the auditor narrative: 

- Deletion verification approach (recommended text): we perform a two-step verification: 1) operational traceability — every delete action produces a delete_job record with unique ID and timestamps across services (API, queue, worker, storage), and 2) post-delete evidence — storage deletion events and object manifest diffs (we keep a short-lived delta manifest for audit sampling). For the SOC 2 artifact we include the delete_job_id and the storage event record.

- Sampling: propose we provide 3 sample delete jobs from tenant-8472 spanning different object types (metadata record, embedding file, and cached session). Auditor asked for minimal artifacts — 3 samples should be sufficient to establish control consistency.

- Retention ledger: we can include a small snippet from our retention ledger (internal runbook reference: RB-RET-2024) that shows retention policy version and who approved it. We should avoid sending full runbooks — include the ledger excerpt and an approval line.

- Exceptions: note that replayed or archived backups beyond TTL are part of our archival policy and covered by a separate escrow/retention agreement. For RedBank explicitly confirm no archival exception is in place for tenant-8472.

I'll draft the verification paragraph for the auditor response; Soojin — can you attach the 3 sample delete jobs (sanitized) and the mapping PDF? Marissa — please confirm the contract/exception point with RedBank legal if needed.

Vivek
Head of Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Lauren Finch <redbank-auditor@assurify.com>, compliance@redbank.com
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-05-07T16:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Evidence request: retention provenance & deletion samples (SOC 2 / ISO)

Hi Lauren / RedBank team —

Thanks for the request. Attached are the artifacts we discussed:
- redwood-retention-mapping-2025-05-07.pdf (compact mapping of object classes -> TTLs -> region)
- sample-delete-log-tenant-8472.csv (sanitized delete job traces; includes delete_job_id and timestamp chain)
- kv-cache-ttl-diagram.png (high-level diagram showing cache boundaries and TTL enforcement)

Summary (what you can expect to validate):
- Object-level TTLs and the geographic mapping are captured in the mapping PDF (tenant-8472 is hosted in us-west1; no cross-region replication is configured).
- The CSV contains 3 sample delete_job traces showing creation_time, delete_request_time, delete_job_id, and deletion_complete_time for different object classes. These can be traced to our storage deletion events.
- Our verification approach combines operational traces (delete_job records) with storage event logs and short-lived manifest diffs. If you require cryptographic hash-based proofs for the deleted blobs we can produce them for a narrow subset after legal/product approval (there is a small operational cost).

If that looks sufficient, can we schedule a 30-min walkthrough next week? I'm available Tue/Wed afternoon PT. Please let me know preferred times and we'll send a calendar invite.

--
Jonas Weber
Director, Compliance Engineering
Redwood Inference
(Attachment stubs: redwood-retention-mapping-2025-05-07.pdf, sample-delete-log-tenant-8472.csv, kv-cache-ttl-diagram.png)
